stories.title: ASU Adding Hotel to its Main Street Entertainment District
stories.excerpt: Arizona State University is adding an upscale hotel in the heart of its Main Street entertainment district. Novus Innovation Corridor will be the site for a seven-story, 116,855-square-foot property that will be part of Marriott Bonvoy’s Tribute Portfolio. The hotel will feature 168 guest rooms, a rooftop pool and bar, and a 2,700-square-foot meeting space. Okland Construction will oversee the hotel’s planning, design and construction management. Sports venue-anchored mixed-use districts are getting national attention for their ability to attract people and increase the value of surrounding properties, and Novus is a leading collegiate example.  ASU is investing more than $150 million in sports venues at Novus, including $55 million in an indoor football practice facility and another $100 million for the modernization of the university’s 51-year-old Desert Financial Arena. That’s on top of the $300 million renovation of Mountain America Stadium and the resounding success of the $140 million, 5,000-seat Mullett Arena.  The post ASU Adding Hotel to its Main Street Entertainment District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ASU investing $150M+ in Novus Innovation Corridor sports venues and infrastructure
168-room Marriott Tribute Portfolio hotel anchoring mixed-use district entertainment expansion
Sports venue-anchored districts drive surrounding property value and foot traffic increases
stories.summary: Arizona State University is developing a 168-room upscale hotel as part of its Novus Innovation Corridor mixed-use district, alongside $150M+ in concurrent sports facility investments including a $300M stadium renovation and new practice facilities. The hotel will be a seven-story, 116,855-square-foot Marriott Bonvoy Tribute Portfolio property with rooftop amenities and meeting space. ASU's multi-hundred-million-dollar sports infrastructure investment is designed to anchor demand in the district and increase surrounding property values.
stories.impact: ASU's concentrated sports and hospitality investment in Tempe signals sustained demand for mixed-use activation around the campus. Multifamily developers should target proximity to Novus—strong daytime/evening foot traffic from students, visitors, and tenants will support above-market rents and faster absorption for student and workforce housing near the corridor.

stories.title: Major Sparks Retail Center Trades for $103M
stories.excerpt: A 41-acre premier mixed-use retail and entertainment destination has traded hands in Sparks, Nevada. Legends at Sparks Marina traded for $103 million. Newmark’s Kyle Miller and Rob Ippolito represented the seller, BIG Shopping Centers USA and RED Development, in the transaction. The property was acquired by Alturas Capital Partners. Located at 1310 Scheels Drive, Legends at Sparks Marina comprises approximately 421,479 square feet and was approximately 95.8% occupied at the time of sale. The center includes Galaxy Theatres, Burlington, H&M, Nike, Sephora, Defy, Cavender’s and the recently announced Yard House, which is currently under development. The property also benefits from adjacent shadow anchors including Scheels, Target, Lowe’s, TJ Maxx and Legends Bay Casino. Ippolito concluded, “Legends at Sparks Marina is uniquely positioned to capitalize on the continued growth of Northern Nevada. The asset offers institutional-quality real estate, strong in-place cash flow and meaningful long-term upside in one of the Western United States’ most dynamic growth markets.” The post Major Sparks Retail Center Trades for $103M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alturas Capital Partners acquired Legends at Sparks Marina for $103M at 95.8% occupancy
41-acre mixed-use retail center in Reno-Sparks region with 421,479 sq ft, anchored by Galaxy Theatres
Northern Nevada positioned as dynamic growth market; buyer cited long-term upside opportunity
stories.summary: Legends at Sparks Marina, a 41-acre, 421,479-square-foot mixed-use retail and entertainment destination in Sparks, Nevada, traded for $103 million with 95.8% occupancy. The asset is anchored by Galaxy Theatres and includes national tenants (Burlington, H&M, Nike, Sephora, Yard House) plus adjacent shadow anchors (Scheels, Target, Lowe's). Alturas Capital Partners acquired the property, with the broker highlighting Northern Nevada's continued growth trajectory and the asset's institutional-quality cash flow and long-term upside.
stories.impact: High-occupancy retail trades at strong prices in Reno-Sparks signal robust consumer demand and demographic migration to Northern Nevada. Multifamily developers should track inbound corporate and population growth in the Reno-Sparks corridor; retail strength at this scale indicates residential demand tailwinds for new apartments, especially workforce and middle-market product near employment nodes and mixed-use centers.

stories.title: S3 Capital Lends $35M for Miami-Dade County Apartments
stories.excerpt: Miami developer Aconcagua Group has landed $35 million of construction financing to complete a multifamily project in Miami-Dade County, Commercial Observer has learned. S3 Capital provided the loan for the third and final phase of the 374-unit Casa Princeton apartment community in Princeton, Fla. The deal closed Friday morning. The phase three portion of the development will comprise an eight-story building with 162 apartments. The second phase Casa Princeton, encompassing 150 units, was delivered in March 2026 and is roughly 40 percent leased, according to S3. “Casa Princeton speaks directly to the attainable housing gap we’re seeing in markets across Florida,” Steven Jemal, managing director of origination at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “The absorption of the initial phases has validated the underlying demand for the product, which gives us conviction as a lender.” Berkadia negotiated the debt with a Miami-based team consisting of Charles Foschini and Christopher Apone. Located at 12835 SW 246th Terrace 30 miles south of Downtown Miami, the apartment community features one and two-bedroom floorplans. Community amenities include a clubhouse, event space, co-working areas, swimming pool, fitness center, playground and dog park. “The Live Local program is a practical example of public policy helping experienced developers deliver more housing where it is needed,” Robert Schwartz, managing principal at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “We’re proud to participate in public-private partnership programs like this, which make it economically possible to increase limited housing supplies and generate value for local communities, developers and our own stakeholders.” Aconcagua Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: S3 Capital closed $35M construction loan for phase three of Casa Princeton, Miami-Dade County
Phase 2 delivered March 2026, 150 units at 40% leased; phase 3 adds 162 units in 8-story building
Lender cites validated demand for attainable housing and strong phase absorption as conviction driver
stories.summary: Aconcagua Group secured $35 million in construction financing from S3 Capital to complete phase three of Casa Princeton in Princeton, Florida (Miami-Dade County), a 374-unit total development. Phase two, delivered in March 2026 with 150 units, is approximately 40% leased; phase three will add 162 units across an eight-story building. The lender cited absorption of initial phases as evidence of underlying demand for attainable housing in the market.
stories.impact: 40% leasing velocity on delivered phase two (within months of delivery) signals strong renter demand for workforce-oriented product in Miami-Dade, particularly in suburban Princeton submarkets. Continued debt availability from S3 Capital for attainable multifamily demonstrates lender confidence in gap-filling housing product; developers should prioritize workforce (60–120% AMI) projects in Miami-Dade suburban nodes where traditional market-rate absorption alone may not support new supply.

stories.title: Amwins Moving Ahead on 15-Story Charlotte Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Amwins Group plans to build a 15-story, 250,000-square-foot office tower at the former Sharon Station site on Sharon Road. The global insurance company asserts the building should cost $39 million. The new tower will feature nine office floors above six parking levels, along with a lobby and approximately 7,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The Charlotte Business Journal reports construction will take 24 to 30 months, and the company plans to begin moving its more than 500 employees into the space before the end of 2028. Its employees will initially occupy seven of the building’s nine office floors, leaving room for future expansion. Currently, the company occupies about 106,000 square feet across six floors at Two Piedmont Town Center, about a mile from the project site. That lease expires in November 2028. Keith Corp is developing the project, while Brasfield & Gorrie will serve as lead contractor. Thrift Commercial Real Estate Services is handling retail leasing for the project. The post Amwins Moving Ahead on 15-Story Charlotte Office Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Amwins Group building 15-story, 250,000 sq ft office tower in Charlotte for $39M, moving 500+ employees
Construction 24–30 months; employees occupy seven of nine office floors by end of 2028; lease expires November 2028
Project anchors former Sharon Station site; retains 1,000+ sq ft ground-floor retail component
stories.summary: Amwins Group, a global insurance company, is developing a 15-story, 250,000-square-foot office tower on the former Sharon Station site in Charlotte for approximately $39 million. The company will consolidate more than 500 employees from six floors at Two Piedmont Town Center (1 mile away) and occupy seven of nine office floors, with buildout targeted for completion before year-end 2028. The tower includes ground-floor retail and will be developed by Keith Corp with Brasfield & Gorrie as lead contractor.
stories.impact: Amwins' investment and consolidation in Charlotte reflects corporate confidence in the market and signals sustained office demand in the Sharon Road submarket. However, for multifamily, the key second-order effect is limited: a 500-person internal relocation does not add net employment to the metro. Monitor if Amwins expansion attracts satellite office tenants or if the Sharon Road retail component becomes a walkable employment/entertainment node that could support nearby residential density.

stories.title: Related Planning Apartments on Site at Fort Lauderdale Office Park
stories.excerpt: Related Group recently paid $9.3 million for a development site at a Fort Lauderdale office park at 6700 N. Andrews Ave. Naya USA was the seller. CPN West retained ownership of the 309,243-square-foot office building there. Last year, Related Group filed plans to develop the vacant portion of this site with apartments. The eight-story Manor Cypress Creek would have 422 apartments and 591 parking spaces. It would include 62 workforce apartments for people making up to 120% of area median income. Amenities would include a pool, a fitness center and an interior courtyard. The S. Florida Business Journal reports this would continue a trend of multifamily development around office buildings in South Florida, as office building owners seek to capitalize on residential demand and make it easier to live near the workplace. bullets: Related Group paid $9.3M for vacant development site at Fort Lauderdale office park, 6700 N. Andrews Ave
Manor Cypress Creek: 422-apartment, 8-story project with 62 workforce units (up to 120% AMI) filed; 591 parking spaces
Trend: multifamily development on office park sites as owners capitalize on residential demand and live-near-work proximity
stories.summary: Related Group acquired a vacant development parcel at a Fort Lauderdale office park (6700 N. Andrews Ave) for $9.3 million, with plans to develop Manor Cypress Creek, an eight-story, 422-unit apartment community including 62 workforce units (targeting up to 120% AMI). The project includes 591 parking spaces, a pool, fitness center, and interior courtyard. This development exemplifies a broader South Florida trend of multifamily layered onto office parks as owners seek to monetize residential demand and create live-near-work opportunities.
stories.impact: Fort Lauderdale office park conversion to residential reflects both office oversupply and strong multifamily demand in South Florida. The inclusion of 62 workforce units (15% of total) indicates lender/local support for affordability. Developers should identify similar underutilized or obsolete office assets in South Florida submarkets (especially Broward/Palm Beach) where ground rent/land acquisition costs are lower than greenfield sites and mixed-use amenity ecosystems can support premium rents.

stories.title: ATC Sells 290-Unit Augusta Apartment Complex
stories.excerpt: Berkadia brokered the sale of MacArthur Park, a 290-unit, garden-style multifamily property in Augusta, Georgia. Christian DiCroce, Jim Sewell, Dave Lansbury, and Erika Maston of Berkadia Charleston led the transaction on behalf of ATC Development, the seller. MacArthur Park sold for $40.6 million and the sales price reflects a per-unit price of $140,000 or $168 per square foot. The property was 91% occupied at the time of the sale. Located at 101 Little Rock Drive, the property affords convenient access to I-520 and U.S. 78, as well as close proximity to Augusta Mall and Fort Gordon. Built in 2022, MacArthur Park features 290 units and a range of community amenities, including a saltwater pool, fitness center, and business center.   ATC has been building apartments in the region for over 50 years. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post ATC Sells 290-Unit Augusta Apartment Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ATC Development sold MacArthur Park, 290-unit garden-style complex in Augusta, Georgia, for $40.6M
Per-unit price $140,000; $168/sq ft; 91% occupied at sale; built 2022 near I-520, Fort Gordon
Berkadia Charleston brokered; property includes saltwater pool, fitness, business center amenities
stories.summary: Berkadia brokered the sale of MacArthur Park, a 290-unit, garden-style apartment community in Augusta, Georgia, built in 2022, for $40.6 million ($140,000 per unit; $168/sq ft). The property was 91% occupied at sale and is located near Interstate 520 and U.S. 78, with proximity to Fort Gordon. The transaction reflects healthy exit velocity for recently built product in secondary markets.
stories.impact: MacArthur Park's 91% occupancy and strong exit valuation in Augusta signal stable demand in the Fort Gordon/military-adjacent submarket. The $140k/unit price in a 2022-built garden product suggests modest cap rates (likely 5–5.5%) still available in secondary metros with demographic anchors. Developers should assess similar military-base-proximate markets (Fayetteville, San Antonio, Jacksonville) where population stability and employment lock-in support reliable absorption.

stories.title: PPM America Provides $236M Acquisition Debt for 20-Property Industrial Deal
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between SparrowHawk and Almanac Realty Investors has secured $236 million in acquisition debt to buy a 4.4 million-square-foot, 20-property U.S. industrial portfolio, according to a release. Fidelity Investments reported earlier that the joint venture purchased the portfolio from EQT for just under $400 million. PPM America provided the $236 million debt, structured as a five-year, fixed-and-floating rate loan, while the JLL Capital Markets team of Brian Walsh, Lucas Borges, Steve Klein, Chris Pratt, Emma Berner and Christian Johnston arranged the transaction. JLL’s Walsh noted in a statement that SparrowHawk has “deep operational expertise” with industrial assets, while he described Almanac Realty Investors as an institutional player with “substantial capital resources.” “This transaction attracted significant lender interest given the institutional quality of the sponsorship and the portfolio’s strategic positioning across high-performing Midwest markets,” Walsh said. Known as “The Central Logistics Portfolio,” the 20-asset assemblage is located across six markets in four states — Kentucky, Ohio, Missouri and Illinois — and is 94 percent occupied by 30 logistics and distribution tenants specializing in different industries. The 20 buildings, on average, opened in 2006 and have an average building size of 221,000 square feet, while the portfolio itself is within a day’s drive of 50 percent of the U.S. population, due to its location in four Midwest states and cities Cincinnati, Columbus, Dayton, Louisville, Cleveland and St. Louis. The deal comes less than a year after SparrowHawk secured a $300 million capital investment from Almanac Realty Investors to finance acquisitions. “The strategic location of these assets across key Midwest markets, combined with JLL’s financing expertise and PPM’s execution, positions us well for long-term growth,” said Alfredo Gutierrez, president and founder of SparrowHawk, in a state
bullets: PPM America provided $236M acquisition debt for SparrowHawk/Almanac Realty 20-property industrial portfolio
4.4M sq ft portfolio purchased from EQT for under $400M; 5-year fixed-floating rate loan structured
Portfolio strategically positioned across high-performing Midwest markets; lenders cited institutional sponsorship quality
stories.summary: A joint venture between SparrowHawk and Almanac Realty Investors acquired a 4.4 million-square-foot, 20-property U.S. industrial portfolio from EQT for just under $400 million, securing $236 million in acquisition financing from PPM America. The debt is structured as a five-year, fixed-and-floating rate loan. The lender highlighted the institutional quality of the sponsorship and the portfolio's strategic positioning across high-performing Midwest industrial markets.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. However, strong debt availability for industrial portfolios at scale signals robust CMBS/life insurance lender appetite. If Midwest industrial demand is heating up (inbound supply chain, manufacturing, logistics reshoring), downstream residential demand in those markets may follow. Developers should monitor industrial absorption trends in Midwest metros (Chicago, Indianapolis, Columbus) as leading indicators of employment stability and wage growth that support new multifamily.

stories.title: Nationwide Life Insurance Company Provides $51M Refi for D.C.-Area Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Zuckerman Gravely has secured $50.75 million to refinance Potomac Place Shopping Center, an 80,000-square-foot, Class-A grocery anchored retail center in Potomac, Md., a suburb just outside of Washington, D.C., Commercial Observer can first report. Nationwide Life Insurance Company provided the debt, structured as permanent fixed-rate financing with a seven-year term. Northmarq’s Jason Smith and Kenneth Gentzel arranged the transaction. In a statement, Smith described the asset as holding a strong retail base with long-time occupants that have generated “robust tenant sales” from a wealthy demographic cohort of residents from Potomac and nearby Chevy Chase and Bethesda, Md. “Located within the heart of Potomac, Maryland, Potomac Place Shopping Center is arguably the most valuable retail center in the region,” said Smith. Located at 10122 River Road in Potomac, near Route-90 and the Washington, D.C., beltway of Highway-495, Potomac Place Shopping Center opened in 1967. Current tenants include Safeway, Walgreens, Starbucks, Chipotle, M&T Bank and PNC Bank. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nationwide Life Insurance provided $50.75M permanent refi for Potomac Place Shopping Center, Maryland
80,000 sq ft Class-A grocery-anchored retail; 7-year fixed-rate term; tenants include Safeway, Walgreens, Starbucks
Asset in affluent Potomac/Chevy Chase/Bethesda submarket near Route-90 and I-495 beltway
stories.summary: Zuckerman Gravely refinanced Potomac Place Shopping Center, an 80,000-square-foot, Class-A grocery-anchored retail center in Potomac, Maryland (near Washington, D.C.), for $50.75 million with Nationwide Life Insurance providing permanent fixed-rate financing over seven years. The asset benefits from long-standing retail tenants (Safeway, Walgreens, Starbucks, Chipotle, M&T Bank) serving the affluent Potomac and nearby Chevy Chase/Bethesda demographic.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. The refi signals continued lender appetite for stable, grocery-anchored retail in affluent D.C. suburbs, but retail refinancing does not signal new residential demand. Monitor if owner/lender appetite to recapitalize this asset suggests interest in ground-up mixed-use (retail + residential) redevelopment in the Potomac corridor, where zoning and demographics support premium rental product.

stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. bullets: Sytes platform connects CRE landlords, developers, brokers with tenants seeking space in real time
Serves 350+ tenants, 35,000+ active listings nationwide; clients include Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, Dutch Bros
Addresses information asymmetry in retail leasing; subscription model; AI leasing agents emerging
stories.summary: Sytes, co-founded by Rafael Weiss, is a commercial real estate marketplace platform that addresses tenant demand visibility problems by connecting landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively seeking space in real time. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active listings across all 50 states, with clients including major REITs and franchisees. The podcast discusses how the platform reduces information asymmetry, tenant filtration, the subscription model, and AI-driven leasing agents.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. Sytes is focused on retail and office tenant placement. However, the broader insight—that demand visibility and real-time tenant matching improve leasing velocity and reduce vacancy—is applicable to multifamily. Developers should adopt similar tenant-demand data platforms and real-time leasing intelligence tools to forecast absorption and optimize unit mix before groundbreaking.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquired four Miami-Dade affordable properties totaling $115.4M and 570 units
Latest acquisitions: Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M) in Little River neighborhood
CBRE/Freddie Mac financing used; prior acquisitions Lafayette Square (160 units, ~$30M) completed last week
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management has completed four acquisitions of affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County totaling $115.4 million and 570 units over two weeks. This week Starwood purchased Lafayette Plaza (136 units, 14-story, $27 million) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6 million), both in the Little River neighborhood. Combined with prior acquisitions of Lafayette Square (160 units) and another property, the portfolio demonstrates institutional capital focus on workforce housing in Miami-Dade. Both recent deals were financed with CBRE-arranged Freddie Mac-backed loans.
stories.impact: Sternlicht's rapid $115M+ accumulation of affordable/workforce housing in Miami-Dade Little River signals three things: (1) institutional conviction that workforce housing (likely 50–80% AMI) in Miami will hold value and generate stable, long-term returns despite rate environment; (2) Freddie Mac's continued appetite for workforce product indicates GSE capital flowing to affordable multifamily; (3) Little River gentrification/density risk is creating demand for preservation/acquisition of existing affordable stock. Developers should focus new construction on workforce product (60–120% AMI) in Miami-Dade, especially in transitioning neighborhoods where land is cheaper and GSE/affordable-focused debt is most available.
